Re-Introduce Ordinance No. 2021-02, which amends Chapter 30.41 Affordable Housing of the Encinitas Municipal Code and the Local Coastal Plan with staff modifications. The draft Ordinance proposes amending the inclusionary housing regulations to increase the inclusionary housing percentage requirements to better address the need for affordable units for all residential development, provide for an in-lieu fee as an alternative method of compliance, and adopt a new affordable housing impact fee for residential care facilities. Staff modification includes additional exemptions for affordable housing impact fee for residential care facilities. Contact Person: Planning Manager Gates
Introduce Ordinance No. 2021-02 titled “An Ordinance of the City of Encinitas, California, Amending Chapter 30.41 Affordable Housing of the Encinitas Municipal Code, which proposes changes to the City’s Inclusionary Housing Regulations including In-Lieu Fee and New Affordable Housing Impact Fee Requirement” as recommended by Planning Commission (Attachment 1 of the agenda report).
2021-09-22 Item 10C Re-introduction of Ordinance 2021-02 Inclusionary Housing

CASE NOS: PLCY-004592-2021; LOCATION: Citywide. Contact Person: Sustainability Manager Najera

2021-09-22 Item 12A Council Initiated Item SB 9 veto
12B.
Council initiated item from Mayor Blakespear and Council Member Hinze regarding adoption of Vision Zero Resolution 2021-91.
1) The City of Encinitas adopts a goal of eliminating traffic deaths and serious injuries by 2028; and endorses Vision Zero as a comprehensive and holistic approach to achieving this goal; 2) The City Council directs the City Manager to form an interdepartmental working group to develop a Vision Zero Action Plan for future consideration by Council, based upon a comprehensive analysis of traffic deaths and injuries in Encinitas which would identify associated funding needed for the City to reach the goal of zero deaths and serious injuries by 2028; 3) The City Council directs the City Manager to ensure that the Vision Zero Action Plan addresses the inequity in traffic deaths and serious injuries through a combination of equitable engineering, enforcement, education, and evaluation; 4) The City Council directs the City Manager to engage the community in the development and implementation of a Vision Zero Action Plan; 5) The City Council directs staff to provide an annual report on implementation of the Vision Zero Action Plan including progress toward eliminating traffic deaths and serious injuries by 2028; 6) The City Council directs staff to submit the Vision Zero Network questionnaire with data supplement; 7) The City Council directs staff to include a provision within the Mobility Element that includes a strategy to evaluate traffic deaths and serious injuries and develop a Vision Zero program that outlines the framework, budget and staffing needed to work towards eliminating pedestrian and bicycle related deaths and serious injuries in Encinitas; and 8) Approve City Council Resolution 2021-91 adopting Vision Zero to achieve zero traffic deaths and serious injuries on Encinitas City Streets by 2028.

Notice to the Public:
To ensure that the City meets your needs when addressing the City Council, all presentation materials which require the use of visual equipment need to be submitted to the City's IT Division at least 24 hours in advance of the meeting (except for appeal hearings where materials must be submitted 7 days in advance). This includes photographs, Microsoft Office documents (PowerPoint, Word, Excel). No CD's, DVD's, or USB thumb/flash drives will be accepted at the meeting. All materials must be in PC format and digital presentation items must be emailed to it-service-desk@encinitasca.gov . Please label all materials with the corresponding agenda item number. Should technical assistance be necessary, it will be available to presenters from 5:30 p.m. to 5:50 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Presentation of video/digital/photographs are considered part of the maximum time limit provided to speakers.
